name: Avenida San Martin and the Centre
tagline: The main street, between the port and the hillside
description: Ushuaia's single commercial street runs parallel to the shore, holding the restaurants, the outfitters, the banks and the tour agencies, with the port and the Antarctic cruise berths a block below. Everything the town offers is on or just off this street.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the outfitters, the restaurants and the port within a few minutes
pros: Every service, agency and restaurant on one street
Port and the Antarctic departures a block away
cons: Crowded with cruise passengers in season
Traffic and noise on the avenue

name: Barrio Brown and the Upper Slopes
tagline: Up the hill, with the Beagle Channel below you
description: The residential streets climbing the slope behind the centre towards the Martial glacier road, where the houses look out over the whole Beagle Channel and the mountains of Navarino island beyond. Quieter than the centre, colder in winter, and the view is the reason people live here.
bestFor: Stays where the channel view out of the window is the point
pros: Uninterrupted views over the Beagle Channel
Quieter than the centre and closer to the ski hill
Walking distance to the Martial glacier trail
cons: Steep streets that ice badly in winter
Ten to fifteen minutes downhill to the shops
Colder and more exposed than the shore

name: Barrio Ecologico and the Western Districts
tagline: The residential west end, where most of the town actually lives
description: The neighbourhoods spreading west along the shore road past the airport turn, where the year-round population lives in ordinary houses and low blocks, with supermarkets, schools and the hospital. Rents here are a fraction of the centre and the bus runs along the main road.
bestFor: Longer stays where the rent matters more than the walk to the restaurants
pros: Supermarkets, the hospital and everyday services nearby
A genuine local neighbourhood rather than a tourist strip
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes into the centre
Exposed to the wind off the channel

name: Bahia Encerrada and the Waterfront
tagline: The sheltered inlet at the eastern end, quiet and close in
description: The eastern end of the town around the enclosed bay, with the coastal path, the airport across the water and newer apartment buildings facing the channel. It is five minutes from the centre on foot, considerably calmer, and the birdlife on the inlet is a daily feature.
bestFor: Stays wanting the water and the coastal path with the centre still walkable
pros: Coastal path and the bay immediately there
Five to ten minutes on foot to San Martin
cons: Aircraft on approach to the airport opposite

name: Tierra del Fuego National Park Road (12 km west)
tagline: Out along Route 3 towards the end of the road
description: The scattered cabins and small lodges along the western road towards the national park entrance, where the forest closes in and the town disappears behind you. Route 3 ends inside the park at Lapataia Bay, and the trails start more or less at the door.
bestFor: Stays built entirely around the park, with a vehicle and no need for the town
pros: National park trails from the doorstep
Complete quiet and southern beech forest
cons: Twenty to twenty-five minutes into town
No shops, and connectivity is poor
